userStories.title: Add resource reservation Pydantic models
userStories.description: As Solar Control, I need typed request/response models for host-local resource reservations across VRAM, RAM, and disk.
acceptanceCriteria: Add solar_host/resources/models.py with WorkloadType enum (training, inference, other)
ReservationRequest includes job_id, optional requester, workload_type, vram_gb, ram_gb, optional disk_gb, and optional ttl_seconds or expires_at (mutually exclusive)
Reservation runtime model includes id (res-<uuid>), created_at, resolved expires_at, and cached actual_vram_gb, actual_ram_gb, actual_disk_gb, usage_polled_at
ResourceDimensionSnapshot includes total_gb, system_used_gb, reserved_headroom_gb, reported_used_gb, available_gb
ResourceSnapshot includes memory_type, per-dimension vram/ram/disk snapshots, and reservations list of ReservationView
ReservationView includes id, job_id, workload_type, status (pending|running), requested and actual per dimension, expires_at
Export public types from solar_host/resources/__init__.py
userStories.notes: All models implemented in solar_host/resources/models.py and exported from __init__.py.

userStories.title: Collect per-job actual resource usage
userStories.description: As the resource manager, I need accurate per-job actual VRAM, RAM, and disk usage so availability math does not double-count running workloads.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend memory_monitor.py with get_gpu_process_memory() returning dict[pid -> bytes] via pynvml compute/graphics running processes
Add DockerService.container_stats(container_id) wrapping container.stats(stream=False)
Add solar_host/resources/usage.py that resolves container PID tree (inspect State.Pid + psutil children) and sums VRAM from pynvml and RAM from memory_stats.usage (minus cache when present)
For disk, measure JOBS_DIR/<job_id> workspace directory size via recursive walk; pending reservations use actual=None
When pynvml is unavailable, VRAM actual is None without failing the host
Blocking Docker/pynvml/psutil calls are suitable for asyncio.to_thread from async callers
userStories.notes: get_gpu_process_memory() added to memory_monitor.py; container_stats() added to DockerService; usage.py fully implemented with all async wrappers.

userStories.title: Implement ResourceManager ledger and availability accounting
userStories.description: As Solar Control, I need the host to track reservations in memory and compute effective availability without overcommitting VRAM, RAM, or disk.
acceptanceCriteria: Add solar_host/resources/manager.py with thread-safe in-memory store keyed by reservation id
create(req) resolves expires_at, validates capacity, and raises CapacityExceededError when reported_used + requested > total for any dimension
Per dimension: reported_usage = system.usage + sum(max(reserved - actual ?? 0, 0)); available = total - reported_usage
Running vs pending derived from JobStore: running iff job_store.get(job_id).status == running
release(id) returns 404 semantics for unknown id and rejects release when linked job is running (409 semantics via exception)
snapshot() returns ResourceSnapshot with live system usage from memory_monitor and get_disk_info
refresh_usage() updates cached actuals for running reservations using active container from JobExecutor and usage.py plus workspace disk size
cleanup_expired(now) removes expired non-running reservations; running reservations never expire via TTL
Reservations are in-memory only (no disk persistence)
userStories.notes: Full implementation in manager.py including CapacityExceededError, ReservationRunningError, refresh_usage_async(), and cleanup_expired().

userStories.title: Expose resource reservation REST endpoints
userStories.description: As Solar Control, I need HTTP endpoints to create, release, and query host-local resource reservations.
acceptanceCriteria: Add solar_host/routes/resources.py with APIRouter and X-API-Key auth inherited from main middleware
POST /resources/reservations returns 201 Created with ReservationView on success
POST returns 422 for invalid body (including both ttl_seconds and expires_at)
POST returns 409 with {error: capacity_exceeded, dimension, requested_gb, available_gb} when capacity exceeded
POST returns 503 when resource manager is unavailable
GET /resources returns 200 ResourceSnapshot including full per-reservation list with per-job actual usage
DELETE /resources/reservations/{id} returns 200 {detail: released, id} on success
DELETE returns 404 for unknown reservation id
DELETE returns 409 when linked job is currently running
Central error-to-HTTP mapping helper mirrors routes/jobs.py patterns
userStories.notes: All endpoints implemented in solar_host/routes/resources.py with correct status codes and error bodies.

userStories.title: Wire ResourceManager and background loops in main.py
userStories.description: As the host process, I need the reservation manager started at boot with periodic usage refresh and expiry cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: Instantiate ResourceManager(job_store, docker_service, job_executor) in lifespan and store on app.state.resource_manager
Start resource_usage_poll_loop (~10s) calling refresh_usage()
Start reservation_cleanup_loop (~60s) calling cleanup_expired(now)
Cancel both loops on shutdown alongside existing health and job cleanup tasks
Register resources router via app.include_router(resources.router)
Host remains usable when Docker is unavailable (snapshots work; running-job actuals may stay None)
